scope: Six purposively selected original development examples; qualitative spot check, not an independent accuracy estimate. No holdout cases used for tuning.

rows.name: Noah Sato
rows.evidence: Electronic sound recordings, audio-layer mixing and a long-running storm-observation notebook.
rows.assessment: Creative discovery is relevant. Art therapy and postsecondary teaching are broad RIASEC connections; there is no established treatment or teaching motivation. Weather and sound interests still need activity-specific discovery beyond this six-score baseline.
rows.action: Keep as exploration invitations; do not relabel therapy or teaching as confirmed Top. Preserve sound/atmospheric directions even when whole-profile r is lower.

rows.name: Owen Mbatha
rows.evidence: Comic performance, bread experiments, biodiversity counts, memorized dialogue and explaining a recipe.
rows.assessment: Performance, arts and experimental work are useful directions. The three strongest therapy/college-teaching connections do not establish a desire to treat clients or teach a subject professionally. Autism and sensory supports supply no career-interest evidence.
rows.action: Offer these for informed exploration, alongside performance and science activities; distinguish teaching interest from explaining one procedure.

rows.name: Cora McIntyre
rows.evidence: Essays, word puzzles, animal records, library discussion and children’s theater.
rows.assessment: Language and narrative options are reasonable to explore. Interpreting/translation needs language-learning or mediation interest; music therapy and speech-language practice are not established by these activities.
rows.action: Show language options without asserting bilingual expertise or clinical motivation; retain writing and animal-data possibilities.

rows.name: Evelyn Duarte
rows.evidence: Running, mythology retellings, quick prioritization and organizing study groups.
rows.assessment: Social and challenging work are plausible broad interests. Rehabilitation and multiple college-teaching specialisms are not confirmed by running or summarizing historical arguments.
rows.action: Use lightweight optional comparisons of learning activities and work contexts; do not turn a high Social score into clinical or subject-specific teaching certainty.

rows.name: Amina Farah
rows.evidence: Strategy games, ethical puzzles, explaining complex rules and sewing costume accessories.
rows.assessment: Creative/social inquiry is grounded. Therapy and special-education results are statistical invitations only; these activities do not establish therapeutic responsibility or working with a particular learner population.
rows.action: Preserve ethics, reasoning, design and community options; avoid substituting the strongest broad correlation for distinctive interest evidence.

rows.name: Mateo Rivas
rows.evidence: Enjoys sound mixing, school cable setup, cooking and bilingual poetry; explicitly avoids long editing sessions.
rows.assessment: Creative and technical exploration is grounded, but a strong statistical Film and Video Editors result conflicts with an explicit preference.
rows.action: Display the conflict and favor setup/audio opportunities for exploration. A broad positive correlation must not erase the specific negative answer.
